title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the Longue Marche notes Grothendieck is studying sections of fundamental-group extensions, i.e. the arithmetic set-up of the section conjecture. The previous page sets up a tower U_S ← U_{O_x} ← U_K over S ← Spec O_x ← K. It also sets up the corresponding cartesian squares of profinite groups E_{U_S} ← E_{U_{O_x}} ← E_{U_K} over E_S ← E_{O_x} ← E_K. He wanted to show that the section φ_x of E_{U_{O_x}} over E_K attached to a K-rational point kills the inertia group I_x. Equivalently, φ comes from a section over E_S if and only if the corresponding rational section is a morphism (is defined at x).

This page. He notes that the statement is purely geometric and local, and reformulates it as a theorem about a trait.
- Setting: T is a trait (spectrum of a discrete valuation ring) with function field K. U/T is a relative 'elementary' scheme, assumed anabelian. A marginal note weakens this to: the fibres are elementary of dimension 1 and U is not A^1, G_m, …, i.e. not of trivial π1.
- Choosing a universal cover Ũ of U fixes an algebraic closure K̄ of K.
- E_U = π1(U; Ũ) is the fundamental group of the total space. E_K = π1(K, K̄) ≅ Gal(K̄/K). E_{U_K} is an extension of E_K by π = π1(U_{K̄}, Ũ).
- These give a square of surjections, E_U ← E_{U_K} over E_S ← E_K. Here E_S = π1(T) is the quotient of E_K by the closed normal subgroup generated by an inertia group I_{x'} ≅ T_∞(K̄)(?).

The next page states the theorem. Let f_K be a K-point of U_K, with associated section ψ: E_K → E_{U_K}. The following are equivalent:
- (a) f_K extends to a section of U over T;
- (b) the composite E_K → E_{U_K} → E_U factors through E_S;
- (b') that composite kills I_{x'}.

The implications (a)⇒(b)⇔(b') are clear. For (b)⇒(a), descent reduces to T strictly local, where E_K is pure inertia and E_S = 1. One then reduces to U = X − D with X a smooth proper relative curve. By properness f extends to X, and one must show f(T) ⊂ U; this is to be done via a lemma on smooth projective relative curves over a strictly local trait.

In modern terms: a K-point of a hyperbolic curve with good reduction (X, D) is integral on U = X − D exactly when its Galois section is unramified. Equivalently, points reducing into the cusps give ramified sections. This is a local 'integral/good-reduction' criterion for Galois sections.
errors: The excluded cases in the margin are slightly over-cautious. The essential exception is U ≅ A^1 (e.g. residue characteristic 0, where π1(A^1_T) = 1 over a strictly local T and (b) holds vacuously). G_m works via Kummer covers ramified at 0 and ∞, so excluding it is harmless but unnecessary.

In mixed or positive residue characteristic the inertia is not pro-cyclic. Writing I_{x'} ≅ T_∞(K̄) is only correct for its tame quotient. The argument via tame Kummer-type covers ramified along D still works, but the identification as written is loose.

ideas.what: Reformulating the local step of the section-conjecture analysis as a purely geometric statement over a trait: a rational point extends to an integral point of U iff its Galois section is unramified.
ideas.modern_name: Good-reduction / integrality criterion for Galois sections; cuspidal sections are ramified
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Tamagawa and Mochizuki (1990s); systematically treated in J. Stix's work on sections of arithmetic fundamental groups (2000s)
ideas.where_published: Not in the Esquisse or the 1983 letter to Faltings as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Square of profinite extensions E_U ← E_{U_K} over E_S ← E_K, with E_S the quotient of the Galois group by its inertia.
ideas.modern_name: Specialization of arithmetic fundamental groups over a DVR

ideas.what: Marginal remark that the anabelian hypothesis can be replaced by: fibres are elementary curves and U is not A^1 (or similar trivial-π1 cases).
ideas.modern_name: Hyperbolicity / non-simply-connected hypothesis for the criterion

missed.claim: Around 1981, Grothendieck formulated (and on the next page sketched a proof of) the criterion that a K-rational point of a relative elementary curve U = X − D over a trait extends integrally iff its Galois section is unramified. This is the local 'integral section' statement later used and proved in the anabelian literature. He also noted that full anabelianity is unnecessary.
missed.quote: Mais il s'agit ici d'un énoncé de fait purement géométrique, que j'ai envie de reformuler sous forme plus générale : Théorème (?) Soit T un trait ... U un schéma relatif "élémentaire" sur T, anabélien*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck already isolated the local integrality step of the section conjecture, the basis of later 'cuspidal sections' and integral-section results. The mathematics itself is now known.

deep.surprise_reason: An early, explicit formulation by Grothendieck of the unramified-section ⇔ integral-point criterion, including the right hypothesis weakening. The result is known in the later literature (Tamagawa, Mochizuki, Stix), so it is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'est la section rationnelle correspondante est morphique' should read 'E_S, ssi la section rationnelle correspondante est morphique'.
The marginal note reads approximately: '* anabélien est inutile — il suffit que les fibres de U soient "élémentaires" de dim 1 et que U ne soit pas ≅ A^1 ou G_m ou (G_m)…, i.e. de π1 nul'.
'une cour[?] extensions de groupes profinis U_K' should read 'un carré d'extensions de groupes profinis'.
The struck-through phrase is '[-section pt K-rationnel de U_K-]'.
In the diagram, the top-left group is E_U (total space) and the top-right is E_{U_K}. The struck text after E_K is '= Gal(K̄/K)'.
'(spectre d'un anneau de valuation discrète[?])': the image shows '(spectre d'un anneau …', which is consistent with this reading.
